page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.6xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the KVM hypervisor. It runs on the x86_64 architecture using an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The instance configuration allocates 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Cache provisions include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache. Memory totals 96.0 GB of RAM, sustaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU.

The hardware configuration includes 4 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. It contains no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached block storage for persistence and OS deployment. Acceleration hardware is omitted, with zero GPUs present. Supported instruction extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, AES cryptography acceleration, BMI2, and FMA, whereas matrix-focused extensions like AMX and VNNI are unavailable.

Benchmark data displays a clear division between single-threaded and parallelized throughput. Due to older Broadwell-era per-core clock architecture, single-core metrics fall into lower percentiles, illustrated by a single-core Geekbench score of 942.0 and single-threaded gzip compression at 19.06 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded evaluations such as the PassMark CPU score of 18419.6, stress-ng multi-core performance of 17646.71, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression reach median levels.

Memory subsystem tests report read throughput at 983.75 GB/sec for small 16 KB cached blocks, 90.83 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads, and 53.0 GB/sec for large sequential writes. In workload-specific benchmarks, the system delivered 16.93 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and a static web serving throughput of 10.83 GB/sec. For lightweight inference, CPU prompt processing reached 1192.97 tokens per second on a 135M model, dropping to 10.47 tokens per second for text generation on a 7B model.

Given its 24-core parallelism and balanced RAM ratio alongside lower single-core frequency, the ecs.sn2ne.6xlarge is cost-effective for multi-threaded batch jobs, enterprise application backends, mid-tier Redis caching, and horizontally scaled web serving, but it is not optimal for single-thread bound pipelines or local I/O intensive databases.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.6xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance equipped with 24 dedicated vCPUs (12 physical cores) powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 96.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, alongside 4 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or hardware accelerators like GPUs. Synthetic and real-world benchmarks reveal standard median multi-core compute and memory bandwidth figures, including 16.93 million Redis SET operations per second and a multi-core Geekbench score of 7212.0. However, single-core throughput remains in the lower quartile due to the clock frequency profile. This makes the instance best aligned with parallelized backend workloads, multi-threaded CI/CD builds, microservices clusters, and general enterprise applications.
